newsitem.title: UK: UK retail petrol industry says lost $184 mln in '96.
newsitem.headline: UK retail petrol industry says lost $184 mln in '96.

text.p: Major oil companies in Britain's refining and marketing industry lost 110 million sterling ($184 million) in 1996 after a pre-tax profit of 94 million sterling in 1995, the U.K. Petroleum Industry Association (PIA) said on Tuesday.

Tight retail margins and overcapacity in the refining sector are expected to continue this year and lead to further downstream consolidation, said Michael Frend, Director General of the PIA, after nearly 10 percent of all U.K. filling stations shut in 1996.
"More mergers, more alliances and more refinery closures," Frend told Reuters. "(The oil companies) do expect 1997 to be a tough year."

British pump prices have lingered in the basement of European rankings after Esso Petroleum launched its Pricewatch campaign in early 1996 promising to match its lowest-priced competitors, industry sources said.
A growing number of hypermarkets selling petrol at the cheapest prices has also favoured drivers of the 22 million cars in Britain and squeezed margins to break-even levels for some retailers.

The 13 members of the PIA, which excludes the independents and hypermarkets, account for 85 percent of the sales volume in the U.K. and the loss comes from its gross sales of 41 billion sterling, including about 20 billion sterling in duties and taxes, he said.
The PIA includes British Petroleum Plc, Conoco, Elf Aquitaine, Esso Petroleum, FINA Inc, Gulf, Kuwait Petroleum Corp, Mobil Corp, Murphy Oil Co, Phillips Petroleum, Shell, Texaco Inc, and Total SA.
-- John Hanley, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8185 ($ = 0.598 British Pounds Sterling)
